fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly on both sides to help responders locate it under low-visibility conditions such as smoke or darkness.
• Clear vegetation along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Trim back any branches overhanging the access drive to allow full-height emergency vehicles to travel without restriction.
• Designate and keep clear a flat, firm area near the main residence where emergency vehicles can turn around without backing long distances down the access drive.
• Keep a secondary turning area near the detached structure clear of equipment, materials, and parked vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation close to the access drive to give arriving responders a clear line of sight to the main residence and detached structure.
• Post a visible site map or address sign near the driveway entrance showing the location of both the main residence and the detached structure.
• Keep a clear path between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot without obstruction.
• If the access drive has a gate, keep it unlocked or install a Knox Box or standard responder lock so units are not delayed at the entrance.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs growing directly next to the structure to create open ground between the plants and the walls.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their branches do not touch or hang over the roof or walls.
• Remove low-hanging branches from trees near the structure so fire cannot climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Cut back ground vegetation along both sides of the driveway to keep it passable for emergency vehicles.
• Trim any tree branches that overhang the driveway so large vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Clear dry or dead ground vegetation from around the base of trees and shrubs near the structure.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the structure free of piled wood, leaves, or loose plant material.
• Thin mixed shrub and tree clusters closest to the structure so there are open gaps between plant groupings.
• Keep the single access route clear of fallen branches, overgrown vegetation, and any debris that could block entry or exit.
• Maintain the open terrain areas near the structure by preventing shrub or ground vegetation from spreading closer to the building over time.
